contract.proof: Ordinary slice updates visit only their owner-local canonicalizer. Response normalization retains one row-ID-to-position index that replaces the former transient duplicate-ID Set; range events perform two expected-O(1) endpoint lookups, scan only the endpoint span, and materialize only leaf IDs from that span. DataGrid reuses the same accepted-view row index instead of retaining a duplicate flat-row index.
contract.adversarialWitness: Two-row tail ranges over 1k, 10k, and 100k accepted domains perform exactly two index lookups and six accepted-row reads in the shared production kernel; the DataTable integration performs no accepted-view filter/map or full-size Array.indexOf.
deterministicWork: ISSUE-062 exercises the shared indexed range kernel at 1k/10k/100k with two Map.get calls and six row reads, plus a public DataTable late-range witness with zero full-view filter/indexOf work.

fullScan.rationale: Ordinary slice updates may validate their external slice but cannot rescan unrelated canonical state.

contract.proof: The current projection generation retains row, column, and cell indexes; a valid adjacent move performs O(1) coordinate lookup and scans only candidates on its movement axis.
contract.adversarialWitness: Every candidate on a 100k-row axis is disabled, forcing one bounded axis scan without rebuilding cell records or indexes.

fullScan.rationale: Canonical movement is bounded to one axis; whole-domain recovery is a separate reconciliation fallback.

contract.proof: Column partitions and one projected index are built once; each header node contributes to one descendant interval exactly once.
contract.adversarialWitness: A maximum-depth header tree with hidden and pinned leaves is visited once and rejects the first non-contiguous group without per-group column scans.

fullScan.rationale: An external column-state replacement must establish the complete header topology invariant once.

variables.name: kRow
variables.meaning: returned access rows excluding context ancestors

variables.name: dContext
variables.meaning: context-only ancestor rows returned with the access slice

assumptions: Application predicate/comparator/group/aggregate/pivot callback internals are external cost; the contract counts library traversals, callback invocations and argument materialization.
contract.proof: Cold resolution normalizes nRecord identities; each enabled filter can visit all records; every sort comparison can walk sSort comparators; pivot discovery materializes the source-record argument once per pivot descriptor; grouping can revisit all records at each group depth; group-cell projection scales with schema columns, aggregate descriptors and materialized pivot columns. Access slicing then emits only kRow plus dContext rows.
contract.adversarialWitness: ISSUE-052 holds nRecord=10 and independently sets filter/sort/group/aggregate/pivot descriptor counts to four: filters and groups perform exactly 40 callbacks, aggregate and pivot policy inputs contain exactly 40 record elements, and equality sorting invokes every comparator descriptor per element comparison. The package benchmark repeats each descriptor axis at counts 1 and 8 with nRecord=1000.

fullScan.rationale: Cold resolution must inspect the external snapshot before producing the first query index.

variables.name: dContext

assumptions: Application callback internals are external cost; changed query/source generations rebuild the same descriptor-sensitive library stages modeled by source.resolve-cold.
contract.proof: A source generation may rebuild normalization and every query/projection stage; a query revision reuses row identities but rebuilds descriptor-sensitive filtering, sorting, grouping, pivot discovery and projection. An expansion revision reuses the prepared query and emits grouped rows under one remaining maxRows budget. The cold worst-case formula therefore remains a safe bound for every invalidation mode.
contract.adversarialWitness: ISSUE-052 varies descriptor counts at fixed records. ISSUE-053 expands a 1,000-record single group under maxRows=1 and rejects before the first leaf/cell projection rather than materializing the subtree.
contract.resourceRationale: Grouped expansion reserves the shared visible-row budget before each group/leaf projection. New leaf/group cache entries are staged locally and merged into the retained query stage only after the complete projection succeeds, so resource rejection does not retain speculative output.

fullScan.rationale: Changed source or query semantics require inspecting the affected current-stage input.

variables.name: dContext
variables.meaning: context-only ancestors required at the slice boundary

contract.proof: Equal source, query, and expansion revisions reuse one retained projection. Flat projections slice directly. Grouped projections retain one 32-bit parent index per row, so a window boundary walks only its ancestor chain and then copies the requested rows; no prefix scan is performed.
contract.adversarialWitness: ISSUE-050 slices the final 10 rows of a 10k flat projection with at most ten numeric row reads and a final nested leaf with exactly two retained ancestor reads plus one output row. The package warm benchmark uses a late offset rather than start=1.

fullScan.rationale: Warm resolution is output-sensitive and cannot rescan the retained source or projection.

contract.proof: Table lookup delegates to the Core Sequence index. Grid lookup combines retained row and column indexes into a row-major coordinate.
contract.adversarialWitness: Repeated last-row and last-column lookup on a large projection performs no Array.indexOf call and retains no cell-ID map.

fullScan.rationale: Locator calls are hot-path identity lookups and must not scan rows, columns, or cells.

variables.name: nColumn
variables.meaning: caller-provided projected column cardinality across all pin partitions

contract.proof: DataTable create/reconcile checks projected row array length before ID mapping. Grid create/reconcile reads row and partition array lengths, checks row/column ceilings, uses division for the projected-cell ceiling, and checks non-empty partition count before mapping row IDs, concatenating column IDs, invoking extent policies, or creating regions.
contract.adversarialWitness: TAB-VIR-09 presents 100k accessor-backed rows at maxProjectedCells=1 to DataTable, DataGrid, and DataTreeGrid create/reconcile and observes zero ID and extent-policy reads. An accessor-backed two-column domain also rejects with zero column element reads; exact-bound one-row/one-column controls remain accepted.

fullScan.rationale: Inputs rejectable from projection cardinality must fail before translating or scanning their identity, extent, or region domains.

variables.name: nRow
variables.meaning: current and next projected row cardinality

variables.name: j
variables.meaning: identity edits required by the bounded sparse repair

contract.proof: A fixed 32-patch planner bounds incremental array and persistent-layout work. Larger diffs use one splice, reuse stable-ID extents from the current indexed domain, and call the extent policy only for new IDs.
contract.adversarialWitness: Reverse order, a large filter, and mixed insertion/removal at 100k rows each produce one bulk mutation; a pure rotation produces one move mutation.

fullScan.rationale: Reconciliation must compare the next identity domain once; it cannot repeatedly scan it per unbounded edit.

assumptions: Virtual replace-track mutations preserve measured extents for stable row and column IDs
current and target endpoint states independently satisfy the retained maxTracks and maxRegions ceilings
ceilings: bounded track unions stop before exceeding maxTracks
fallback bridge regions are a subset of the current region domain
every emitted row/column track replacement is an endpoint-sized domain
contract.proof: Reconciliation attempts the existing union bridge only while each union fits maxTracks. If either union would exceed the retained track ceiling, the adapter keeps only regions whose row and column IDs exist in both endpoints, directly replaces endpoint-sized row and column tracks through Virtual's extent-preserving mutations, then installs target regions. A constant number of complete endpoint/region traversals is performed and no intermediate Virtual track state exceeds maxTracks.
contract.adversarialWitness: TAB-VIR-08 reconciles disjoint two-row and disjoint two-column endpoints at maxProjectedCells=2, where the old union cardinality is four. Both direct target constructions and DataGrid/DataTreeGrid reconciliations succeed, every emitted track/region mutation remains at or below two items, and a shared measured row/column retains its exact extent through the bounded fallback.

fullScan.rationale: Grid reconciliation must compare current and target track domains and may filter the current region set once to construct a ceiling-safe bridge; it may not construct or retain a track domain larger than the endpoint ceiling.
